Subject: Capacity planning & MAP for Dedicated/private lead times

Hi Kimberly,

We're kicking off our evaluation for inference at Stellarnet and want to line up a mutual action plan that covers timelines for Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) deployments and an initial GPU pool sizing recommendation. High level: we expect to run 6–8k QPS-weft-like workloads during peak model runs and want a predictable cost / SLA path.

Key asks from our side to start the MAP:
- Typical lead time to provision a Dedicated GPU pool (H100) vs a private on-prem installation (full network/vpc + install).
- Pilot sizing guidance (pilot -> scale) and recommended guardrails for model quantization or batching to reduce capacity.
- Any documents you need from procurement / security to speed the contract + onboarding.

We'd like to run a 4–8 week eval (POC) with a short production gate after acceptance. Can you propose a MAP with milestones and a realistic close timeline? Procurement contact is procurement@stellarnet.ai — I can loop them in once there's a timeline.

Thanks,
Alyssa Park

Hi Alyssa — great to hear from you and congrats on moving toward production-grade inference. I've attached a quick MAP template (MAP-Stellarnet-v1.xlsx) and a short GPU sizing snapshot. Below is a suggested plan we can iterate on.

Proposed high-level MAP (draft)
- Week 0: Kickoff + requirements capture (SLOs, workloads, security needs)
- Week 1–4: Evaluation (access to hosted sandbox / Dedicated pilot)
   - Pilot options: 8 H100s (short pilot), or mixed pilot 4 H100 + 16 A100 for cost/throughput tradeoffs
   - Acceptance: throughput and P95 latency gates + functional checks on KV caching and prefix reuse
- Week 5–8: Scale plan & procurement alignment (mutual acceptance -> reserve 24 H100s dedicated OR deploy Private on-prem)
- Week 9–16+: Provisioning and cutover (Dedicated typical lead time ~8–12 weeks after PO; Private on-prem build ~14–22 weeks depending on rack/hw lead times and network approvals)

GPU sizing guidance (quick):
- Conservative launch (lower unit cost, faster to provision): 24 H100s Dedicated pool — best uniform performance for large-context LLMs
- Cost-balanced: mixed pool (16 H100s + 48 A100s) — keeps cost down for embedding/embedding-heavy routes and uses H100s for latency-sensitive generation
- Pilot recommendation: Start with a 12-H100 pilot (we've found this gives good signal on perf and tail latency without a large upfront commitment).

Procurement/security asks to attach to MAP:
- Procurement: PO cadence, legal lead, standard PO terms, billing contact (attach procurement@stellarnet.ai)
- Security: SOC 2, data residency expectations, KMS/HSM requirements; we will share SOC2 Type II report and a checklist.

Attachments: MAP-Stellarnet-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB); GPU-sizing-projection-3Q2026.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

Next steps: if you confirm pilot sizing (8/12 H100) we'll schedule an engineering kickoff and lock in a pilot window. I'll loop Rishi to confirm provisioning and Priyom to scope the eval engineering support.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — quick technical note from capacity/ops perspective:

- Pilot sizing tradeoffs: an 8 H100 pilot gives us good latency signal but may underexpose scaling contention patterns (KV cache hit ratios, concurrent KV eviction). A 12 H100 pilot is a better minimum if you want to validate P95 under 75% of expected peak.
- Fallbacks: we can provide a quantized model variant (4-bit) to reduce required GPUs by ~2–2.5x for throughput-bound routes. This is an ops-level mitigation that helps if procurement/lead times delay provisioning.
- Provisioning lead times (ballpark): Dedicated (redwood-managed): 8–12 weeks after signed PO for H100 procurement + allocation; Private (customer-managed on-prem): 16–22 weeks (hardware lead times + site acceptance + rack & network). We should build in a 2-week buffer for SOC2 checklist completion & legal redline cycles.

Operational ask for MAP:
- Procurement contact + preferred PO terms (Net 30 vs Net 60), and whether Stellarnet requires vendor-side NDA-limited billing fields.
- Confirm whether the pilot must be in VPC (private) or if a hosted dedicated pilot is acceptable (hosted is usually much faster to stand up).

I'll draft a provisioning window and a runbook once we confirm pilot size and whether it's hosted or private.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Dedicated Solutions | Redwood Inference
